title: Wavefront sets, Hadamard kernels and admissible local products

items.title: Scalar distributions on smooth manifolds
items.statement:
In positive dimension use the Euclidean test-function spaces and their topology from the suppliers below. In dimension zero put $\mathbb R^0=\{*\}$ and declare every complex-valued function on either open subset smooth. Define $\mathcal D(\{*\})=\mathbb C$ by evaluation at $*$, with its usual absolute-value norm topology, and $\mathcal D(\varnothing)=\{0\}$ with its unique topology. Define $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ in this dimension as the continuous complex-linear dual of $\mathcal D(\Omega)$: on $\{*\}$ its elements are exactly $f\mapsto cf(*)$, $c\in\mathbb C$, and on the empty set there is only zero. The unique zero-dimensional multi-index has order zero and its derivative is the identity; an empty determinant and the density symbol $|dx^1\cdots dx^0|$ both equal one.

Let $M$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable smooth $n$-manifold without boundary. In a smooth chart $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, a smooth density is written $\phi_x(x)|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$. On a coordinate change $y=\psi(x)$ its coefficient transforms by
$$ \phi_y(y)=\phi_x(\psi^{-1}(y))\,|\det D\psi^{-1}(y)|. $$
A compactly supported smooth density is one whose support (the closure of the set where its coefficient is nonzero) is compact in $M$. For compact $K\subset M$, let $\mathcal D_K(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)$ be the complex vector space of smooth densities supported in $K$. For every chart $x:U\to\Omega$, compact $L\subset U$, and integer $r\ge0$, give this space the seminorm
$$p_{x,L,r}(\omega)=\max_{|\alpha|\le r}\sup_{z\in x(L)}|\partial^\alpha\phi_x(z)|.$$
An empty supremum is zero. These seminorms define the fixed-support locally convex topology. On the union $\mathcal D(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)=\bigcup_{K\text{ compact}}\mathcal D_K(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)$, take all seminorms whose restriction to every fixed-support space is continuous; their finite intersections of open seminorm balls and translates define the test-density topology. Thus it is the finest locally convex topology making every fixed-support inclusion continuous, as in the Euclidean test-function topology. This specifies the locally convex inductive limit without choosing an exhaustion.

A scalar distribution on $M$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on this space, with bilinear pairing $\langle u,\omega\rangle$. Write $\mathcal D'(M)$ for these distributions. The support of $u$ is the complement of the union of open sets on which it annihilates every supported test density; $\mathcal E'(M)$ denotes those with compact support. For $x:U\to\Omega$, its coordinate representative is defined for $f\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ by
$$\langle u_x,f\rangle=\langle u,\widetilde{x^*(f|dz^1\cdots dz^n|)}\rangle,$$
where the tilde extends the density by zero outside $U$. This extension is smooth because the support is compact in $U$. On each fixed support its derivatives in any other chart are bounded by finitely many derivatives of $f$, by the chain and product rules on compact sets; hence the extension map is continuous for the specified topologies and $u_x$ is a Euclidean distribution. In dimension zero derivatives have order zero and the density determinant is one. On a product manifold use the same definition with product densities. For a smooth diffeomorphism $f:N\to M$, define $f_*\omega=(f^{-1})^*\omega$ for test densities, using the displayed absolute-Jacobian rule. Define its distributional pullback by $\langle f^*u,\omega\rangle=\langle u,f_*\omega\rangle$. Compact supports are mapped to compact supports, and the same compact derivative estimates prove continuity. This includes coordinate changes and interchange of factors of a product.

items.title: Local Fourier definition of a wavefront set
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $u\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$, using the local distribution convention of [[def-qftx-distributions-on-smooth-manifolds]]. For $p\in\Omega$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$, call $(p,\xi)$ regular for $u$ if there are $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\chi=1$ near $p$ and an open cone $\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ containing $\xi$ such that for every integer $N\ge0$,
$$ \sup_{\eta\in\Gamma}(1+|\eta|)^N\left|\left\langle u,\chi(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\eta}|dx^1\cdots dx^n|\right\rangle\right|<\infty. $$
The local wavefront set $\operatorname{WF}_\Omega(u)$ is the complement of these regular pairs in $T^*\Omega\setminus0$, with the standard cotangent coordinates $(p,\xi)$. A cone is invariant under multiplication by positive scalars. This is a chart-level definition; this item makes no assertion about its behavior under a change of coordinates.

items.title: Wavefront and positive-frequency Hadamard data
items.statement:
Let $M$ first be any Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary and $u\in\mathcal D'(M)$. No metric, orientation or dimension restriction is used in the following wavefront definition. For each smooth chart $x:U	o\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $u_x\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ be the coordinate representative of $u$ in the test-density convention. Map a local covector $(x(p),\xi)\in T^*\Omega$ to $(p,dx_p^T\xi)\in T^*M$. Define the global wavefront set by the union over all charts,
$$ \operatorname{WF}(u):= igcup_{(U,x)}\{(p,dx_p^T\xi):(x(p),\xi)\in\operatorname{WF}_{x(U)}(u_x)\}\subset T^*M\setminus0, $$
where the local sets are the local Fourier wavefront sets. Thus the global set is defined using all charts; equality of the chartwise descriptions on overlaps is a separate theorem. The Fourier convention is the displayed $2\pi$ convention.


Let $(M,g)$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented, time-oriented, globally hyperbolic smooth Lorentzian $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\ge2$. Here $g$ is a smooth symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form on each tangent space with one negative and $n-1$ positive directions; in charts its signature is $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. An orientation is a smooth choice of orientation in each tangent space. A time orientation selects one of the two components of $\{v
e0:g(v,v)<0\}$ as future. A tangent vector is causal when $g(v,v)\le0$, and is future or past causal when it belongs to the closure of the selected future or past timelike cone. A future causal curve is a continuous map $c:I	o M$, where $I\subset\mathbb R$ is an interval, which is piecewise $C^1$ on each compact subinterval, with finitely many pieces there and nonzero future causal tangent on each smooth piece. Past curves are defined with the opposite cone. Endpoint values, when included in $I$, are taken by continuity. Define $J^+(p)$ by including $p$ and all $q$ for which a future causal curve $c:[a,b]	o M$, $a<b$, has $c(a)=p$, $c(b)=q$; put $J^-(p)=\{q:p\in J^+(q)\}$. Here globally hyperbolic means strongly causal and every causal diamond $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; strongly causal means every point has arbitrarily small neighborhoods which each causal curve meets in a connected parameter interval. A nonzero cotangent vector is future or past causal, or future or past null, when its metric dual under $g^{-1}$ has the corresponding tangent property.

Functional-kernel pairings and contractions on this page use $\mu_g$ in each integrated variable; no physical units are assigned.


Write $

abla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma=0$; it is future-directed when $\dot\gamma$ lies in the chosen future causal cone. Two nonzero future-null cotangent vectors $(p,\xi)$ and $(q,\zeta)$ are related, written $(p,\xi)\sim(q,\zeta)$, if $p=q$ and $\zeta=\xi$, or if there are a nonconstant future-directed affinely parametrized null geodesic $\gamma:I	o M$, parameters $s,t\in I$ in either order, and a common scale $\lambda>0$ such that
$$p=\gamma(s),\qquad q=\gamma(t),\qquad \xi=\lambda g_p(\dot\gamma(s),\cdot),\qquad \zeta=\lambda g_q(\dot\gamma(t),\cdot).$$
These covectors are the metric-dual tangents to that geodesic and are related by induced covector parallel transport. There is no requirement $s\le t$: the future-frequency choice concerns the covectors, not an ordering of the two base points. There is no complex conjugation. Integration by parts characterizes it intrinsically by $\int (Pf)\omega=\int f(P^{\mathrm t}\omega)$ for every smooth scalar $f$ and test density $\omega$; hence coordinate expressions agree. items.title: Wavefront sets are invariant under smooth coordinate changes
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For a distribution $u$ on a smooth manifold, the chartwise rapid-decay definition of its wavefront set is independent of the chart: if $y=\psi(x)$, its covector coordinates satisfy $\eta=(D\psi(x))^{-T}\xi$. The resulting $\operatorname{WF}(u)$ is closed and conic in $T^*M\setminus0$. For distributions $u,v$ and a smooth diffeomorphism $\psi$, one has $\operatorname{WF}(u+v)\subseteq\operatorname{WF}(u)\cup\operatorname{WF}(v)$ and $\operatorname{WF}(\psi^*u)=\psi^*\operatorname{WF}(u)$. Finally, $\operatorname{WF}(u)=\varnothing$ exactly when $u$ is represented by a smooth scalar function in every chart.

items.title: Compactly supported polynomial microcausal functionals
items.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented, time-oriented, globally hyperbolic smooth Lorentzian $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\ge2$, with signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. A cotangent vector is future or past causal when its metric dual belongs to the corresponding closed causal tangent cone. For $r\ge1$, let $\overline V_\pm^r\subset T^*M^r\setminus0$ consist of tuples $(x_1,\ldots,x_r;\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r)$ such that every $\xi_j$ is either zero or future causal for $+$, respectively past causal for $-$, and the total tuple is nonzero. The wavefront set used below is the set of nonzero cotangent tuples where compactly localized Fourier transforms fail rapid decay in every conic neighborhood.

A compactly supported polynomial functional is a finite expression
$$ F(\phi)=\sum_{m=0}^{N}\left\langle f_m,\phi^{\otimes m}\mu_g^{\otimes m}\right\rangle, $$
where $\phi\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$, $f_m\in\mathcal E'(M^m)$ is symmetric under permutations of its $m$ variables, $\mu_g$ is the metric density fixed by the Lorentzian metric, and the pairing is defined by inserting a compactly supported cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}f_m$ in the smooth factor. Its $r$th functional derivative $F^{(r)}(\phi)\in\mathcal E'(M^r)$ is specified, for a test density $\omega$ on $M^r$, by
$$ \left\langle F^{(r)}(\phi),\omega\right\rangle =\sum_{m=r}^{N}\frac{m!}{(m-r)!} \left\langle f_m,\omega\otimes\phi^{\otimes(m-r)}\mu_g^{\otimes(m-r)}\right\rangle, $$
where a compactly supported cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}f_m$ is inserted in the smooth $\phi$ factors. Expanding the finite polynomial shows that this kernel represents the directional derivative in smooth compactly supported real directions. The functional is microcausal when
$$ \operatorname{WF}(F^{(r)}(\phi))\cap(\overline V_+^r\cup\overline V_-^r)=\varnothing $$
for every $r\ge1$ and every $\phi\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$. Write $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(M)$ for this class, including constants.

items.title: Canonical global microlocal pullback by controlled local Fourier construction
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $M,N$ be Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifolds without boundary, let $f:N\to M$ be smooth, and let $\Gamma\subset T^*M\setminus0$ be closed and conic. Put
$$N_f=\{(f(x),\eta):\eta\ne0,\ df_x^T\eta=0\}.$$
If $\Gamma\cap N_f=\varnothing$, every $u\in\mathcal D'(M)$ with $\operatorname{WF}(u)\subset\Gamma$ has a canonical scalar-distribution pullback $f^*u$. It agrees with $u\circ f$ for smooth scalar functions, commutes with restriction to open subsets, is independent of all coordinate charts and support cutoffs, and satisfies
$$\operatorname{WF}(f^*u)\subset f^*\Gamma:=\{(x,df_x^T\eta):(f(x),\eta)\in\Gamma\}.$$
In particular the same assertion holds with $\Gamma=\operatorname{WF}(u)$. A nonproper map and a test whose image meets several target charts are allowed.

The following precise local convergence property is part of the assertion. Call $u_j\to u$ **controlled relative to $\Gamma$** when all these distributions have wavefront sets in $\Gamma$, they converge on every fixed test density, on each fixed compact test support they share one finite derivative-order bound, and, in every chart, for every compact smooth cutoff $a$ and closed cone $C$ with $(\operatorname{supp}a\times C)\cap\Gamma=\varnothing$, one has
$$\sup_j\sup_{\eta\in C}(1+|\eta|)^q|\widehat{a u_j}(\eta)|<\infty\qquad(q=0,1,\ldots).$$
An empty cone imposes no condition. Then $f^*u_j\to f^*u$ is controlled relative to $f^*\Gamma$ locally, with common support bounds whenever the input supports and the relevant source test supports are fixed. On a compact coordinate patch, compactly supported smooth mollifications of a localized distribution give such an approximating sequence on every smaller patch. Consequently the pullback is uniquely determined by its smooth values and this controlled sequential continuity. This statement uses the explicitly defined convergence property, rather than assuming a general spectral or locally convex extension principle.

items.title: Product and pullback under wavefront transversality
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $u\in\mathcal D'(M)$, where $M$ is a smooth manifold. For a smooth map $f:N\to M$, define its nonzero conormal set by
$$ N_f=\{(f(x),\eta)\in T^*M\setminus0: df_x^T\eta=0\}. $$
If $\operatorname{WF}(u)\cap N_f=\varnothing$, there is a distributional pullback $f^*u\in\mathcal D'(N)$ and
$$ \operatorname{WF}(f^*u)\subseteq \{(x,df_x^T\eta):(f(x),\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)\}. $$
For $u,v\in\mathcal D'(M)$, if there is no nonzero covector $\eta$ with both $(x,\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)$ and $(x,-\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(v)$ at the same $x$, their product is defined by $uv=\Delta^*(u\otimes v)$, where $\Delta(x)=(x,x)$. It agrees with pointwise multiplication when $u,v$ are smooth and satisfies
$$ \operatorname{WF}(uv)\subseteq \{(x,\eta+\zeta):(x,\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)\cup0_M,\ (x,\zeta)\in\operatorname{WF}(v)\cup0_M,\ \eta+\zeta\ne0\}. $$
Here $0_M$ is the zero section. If $\pi:X\times Y\to X$ is a coordinate projection, $\nu$ is a smooth positive density on $Y$, and $t\in\mathcal E'(X\times Y)$, define $\pi_{*,\nu}t$ by
$$ \langle \pi_{*,\nu}t,\omega\rangle =\left\langle t,\chi(\pi^*\omega\otimes\nu)\right\rangle, $$
where $\omega$ is a compactly supported test density on $X$ and $\chi$ is a compact cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}t$. This pushforward is independent of $\chi$, compactly supported, and
$$ \operatorname{WF}(\pi_{*,\nu}t)\subseteq \{(x,\eta):\text{ for some }y,\ (x,y;\eta,0)\in\operatorname{WF}(t)\}. $$
The pullback condition is a local transversality requirement; this theorem does not define an arbitrary restriction of a singular kernel to a diagonal where the condition fails.

items.title: Canonical compatibility of microcausal cross contractions and smooth self contractions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold, density $\mu_g$ and positive-frequency Hadamard relation of [[def-qftx-wavefront-hadamard]]. Let $a\in\mathcal E'(M^p)$ and $b\in\mathcal E'(M^q)$, $p,q\ge0$, be polynomial coefficient kernels whose nonzero wavefront tuples avoid the all-future and all-past causal cones, with zero entries allowed in those cones. Degree-zero kernels are scalars. Label their slots by two distinct original blocks, $A$ and $B$.

Take a finite matching of some of the $p+q$ labelled slots: each slot belongs to at most one edge. Each singular edge joins one slot of $A$ to one slot of $B$, in that order, and has kernel $W$ with $\operatorname{WF}(W)\subseteq\mathcal C_g^+$. Every other edge has a smooth kernel on $M^2$; such an edge may join two slots within either original block or cross between the blocks. No symmetry of these smooth kernels is required for the construction. Multiply $a\otimes b$ by these pulled-back edge kernels and integrate each matched variable against $\mu_g$, retaining the unmatched slots as output variables.

This prescription gives a canonical compactly supported distribution on the unmatched slots. All products and intermediate integrations required by any ordering of these edge contractions are admissible and give the same result as the simultaneous prescription. Here an edge contraction removes its two distinct labelled original slots; no operation duplicates an original coefficient kernel or contracts a removed slot again. The conclusion also includes first contracting smooth edges in each input and then making cross-block singular contractions. The output kernel again avoids the two microcausal cones. Permuting labelled slots or differentiating a finite polynomial functional in external smooth directions gives the corresponding permutation or finite Leibniz expansion of these same kernels.

Consequently all coefficientwise rearrangements of cross-factor $D_W$ contractions and smooth $\Gamma_K$ contractions used in the Hadamard-change formula are canonical on compactly supported polynomial microcausal functionals. This statement does not define a self-contraction $\Gamma_W$ on that class: a mixed future/past wavefront tuple of an individual coefficient need not be transverse to a singular two-point kernel.

items.title: Hadamard contractions preserve microcausal polynomial functionals
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $\hbar$ be a formal indeterminate. Let $W\in\mathcal D'(M\times M)$ be a scalar Hadamard bisolution. For $F,G\in\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(M)$, let $\deg F$ be the largest degree with nonzero coefficient kernel, with $\deg 0=0$, and define, coefficientwise in $\hbar$,
$$ F\star_W G =\sum_{r=0}^{\min(\deg F,\deg G)} \frac{\hbar^r}{r!} \left\langle F^{(r)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(r)}(\phi),\,W^{\otimes r}\right\rangle. $$
Each term is formed by the distribution product on the $r$ contracted variable pairs and proper pushforward over those pairs, as in [[thm-qftx-wavefront-product]], integrating with the metric density $\mu_g$ in each contracted variable. The sum is finite and defines a member of $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(M)\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$. If $K\in C^\infty(M\times M)$ is symmetric, then
$$ \Gamma_KF(\phi)=\left\langle F^{(2)}(\phi),\chi K\mu_g^{\otimes2}\right\rangle $$
is also a compactly supported polynomial microcausal functional and lowers polynomial degree by two; here $\chi$ is any compactly supported cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}F^{(2)}(\phi)$.

items.title: Smooth Hadamard changes intertwine the polynomial microcausal products
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $W,W'\in\mathcal D'(M\times M)$ be scalar Hadamard bisolutions for the same $(M,g,P)$ and the same positive-frequency null relation, with
$$ W-W^{\mathsf T}=W'-W'^{\mathsf T}=iE $$
for one fixed distribution $E$. Then $K:=W'-W$ is a smooth symmetric function on $M\times M$. For every compactly supported polynomial microcausal functional $F$, define
$$ \Gamma_KF(\phi)=\left\langle F^{(2)}(\phi),\chi K\mu_g^{\otimes2}\right\rangle,\qquad \alpha_K=\exp\!\left(\frac{\hbar}{2}\Gamma_K\right) =\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{(\hbar/2)^j}{j!}\Gamma_K^j. $$
Here $\chi$ is any compactly supported cutoff equal to one near the compact support of $F^{(2)}(\phi)$, and $\mu_g$ is the metric density. The sum is finite on each $F$, $\alpha_K$ is bijective with inverse $\alpha_{-K}$, and, coefficientwise in the formal parameter $\hbar$,
$$ \alpha_K(F\star_WG)=\alpha_KF\star_{W'}\alpha_KG $$
for all $F,G\in\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(M)$. No existence of $W$ or $W'$ is asserted.

items.title: Delta-square is outside the product contract
items.statement:
The universal assertion that the wavefront product criterion defines $\delta_0^2$ is false. In $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, the Dirac distribution $\delta_0$ has $\operatorname{WF}(\delta_0)=\{(0,\xi):\xi\ne0\}$, so the criterion excludes its product with itself. Moreover, for any nonnegative unit-mass radial mollifier $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ supported in $B_1(0)$, the ordinary smooth squares $\rho_\varepsilon^2$, where $\rho_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-n}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$, have no distributional limit as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ without subtraction: for every test function $f$ equal to one near zero and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,
$$ \langle \rho_\varepsilon^2,f\rangle =\varepsilon^{-n}\int_{\mathbb R^n}\rho(y)^2\,dy\longrightarrow+\infty. $$
This does not rule out a separately specified renormalized extension; it shows that neither the stated product criterion nor this unrenormalized mollifier limit supplies one.
